question.problem:
Fill in the blanks to make the following reasoning true.

Since $\text{gcd}(69,82)=$
{{field-1}}, 
by the extended Euclidean algorithm, we have 

| $1\,=\,69\,\cdot ($
{{field-2}}

{{field-3}}

Therefore, ${69}^{-1}\,\text{mod}\,82=$
{{field-4}} (expressed as the smallest nonnegative residue).
question.worked_solution:
First of all, notice that $\text{gcd}(69,82)=1.$ So, the multiplicative inverse of $69$ modulo $82$ exists.

The multiplicative inverse of $69$ modulo $82$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
69\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,82).
$$

To find the value of $x,$ we will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}82 & = & 69\cdot 1 & + & 13 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 69 & = & 13\cdot 5 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 13 & = & 4\cdot 3 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =82-69 \\ 4 & =69-13\cdot 5 \\ 1 & =13-4\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =13-4\cdot 3 \\  & =13-(69-13\cdot 5)\cdot 3 \\  & =13-69\cdot 3+13\cdot 15 \\  & =13\cdot 16-69\cdot 3 \\  & =(82-69)\cdot 16-69\cdot 3 \\  & =82\cdot 16-69\cdot 16-69\cdot 3 \\  & =82\cdot 16-69\cdot 19 \\  & =69\cdot (-19)+82\cdot 16\end{aligned}
$$

We can write this result modulo $82,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}69\cdot (-19)+82\cdot 16 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82) \\ 69\cdot (-19) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82) \\ 69\cdot (82-19) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82) \\ 69\cdot 63 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $69\cdot 63≡1\,(\text{mod}\,82),$ which means that ${69}^{-1}\,\text{mod}\,82=63.$
